keyframe_review.note: New one-year keyframe: Philip II conquered Poitou in 1205 ('Poitou was conquered by King Philip II of France in 1205'); Cliopatria's first Poitou shape begins in 1206. The region is the corrected 1206 shape.

correction.text: Poitou: Vendée, Deux-Sèvres and Vienne instead of Cliopatria's south-western block

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's shape (1206..1240, 23,634 km2) lies south-west of the page's Poitou: in the gazetteer it holds all of Charente (25/25 cells, the Angoulême the page names as a neighbouring county) and 10/29 of Charente-Maritime, but only 11/25 of Deux-Sèvres and 11/27 of Vienne cells (Vendée 25/29). The page's Poitou, 'Vendée, Deux-Sèvres, Vienne', is 81 gazetteer cells (about 20,485 km2), ratio 0.87 to Cliopatria's 23,634 km2; the infobox shows no area. Replace the shape by the region Poitou.

correction.text: Poitou: Vendée, Deux-Sèvres and Vienne, Alphonse of Poitiers' apanage

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's shape (1241..1249, the same polygon as 1206) lies south-west of the page's Poitou: in the gazetteer it holds all of Charente (25/25 cells, the Angoulême the page names as a neighbouring county) and 10/29 of Charente-Maritime, but only 11/25 of Deux-Sèvres and 11/27 of Vienne cells (Vendée 25/29). The page's Poitou, 'Vendée, Deux-Sèvres, Vienne', is 81 gazetteer cells (about 20,485 km2), ratio 0.87 to Cliopatria's 23,634 km2; the infobox shows no area. Replace the shape by the region Poitou. No page opened dates a 1241 change: the Alphonse page gives 'Count of Poitou from 1225' and the County of Auvergne page 'In 1225, Louis VIII ... granted Poitou and Auvergne to his third son Alfonso'; the shape keeps the same area.

correction.text: Poitou unchanged, Alphonse of Poitiers' apanage until his death in 1271

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1250..1271: Cliopatria drops Poitou in 1250, but Alphonse stays Count of Poitiers to 1271 (infobox 'Reign: 1225–1271', died at Savona on 21 August 1271) and the County of Auvergne page says Poitou 'reverted to the royal domain' on his death in 1271. The corrected region is unchanged. The kingdom-of-france dossier's 1250 gain of Poitou should move to 1271 or be read as the same land.

ledger.note: 1205: Philip II Augustus conquers Poitou from the English crown. 'Poitou was conquered by King Philip II of France in 1205 after he declared it a confiscated fief of the crown.' Infobox: 'In personal union with the Kingdom of England; (1154-1205)'. The page gives the year, not the month; Cliopatria's first Poitou shape begins in 1206.

1225: Louis VIII grants Poitou to his third son Alfonso (Alphonse of Poitiers), who holds it as an apanage; same state, same colour. 'In 1225, Louis VIII of France granted Poitou and Auvergne to his third son Alfonso.' The Alphonse page's infobox gives 'Count of Poitiers, Reign: 1225–1271' and the text 'was the Count of Poitou from 1225'. Cliopatria's second shape begins in 1241, a date no page opened gives (the area does not change).

region.text: Poitou reverting to the royal domain

ledger.note: 1271: Alphonse dies and Poitou reverts to the royal domain. 'On Alfonso's death in 1271, Auvergne, along with the County of Toulouse, Poitou and the Comtat Venaissin' reverted to the royal domain (page text, sentence cut at 125 characters by the reader). Alphonse died at Savona on 21 August 1271 (Alphonse page, second page). He had become Count of Toulouse in 1249 ('they became rulers of Toulouse at Raymond's death in 1249'); Cliopatria ends Poitou then, but the pages keep it a separate apanage to 1271.

wars.name: Philip II's conquest of Poitou
wars.outcome: Philip II declared Poitou a confiscated fief and conquered it in 1205; the English crown lost the county.
wars.note: The page also names the Saintonge War, in which Henry III failed to retake Poitou, but gives it no date; not entered as a dated war.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey on the pages opened; the extent is the page's three sub-regions and the bordering counties it names, drawn as a soft feudal frontier.

notes:
Settled from pages: conquest by Philip II in 1205 (County of Poitou); Alphonse count 1225-1271 (Alphonse; County of Auvergne); reversion to the royal domain in 1271 (County of Auvergne).
Cliopatria problems: (1) the polygon is not Poitou: it is a south-western block holding all of Charente (the Angoulême the page lists as a neighbouring county) and only about half of Deux-Sèvres and Vienne; all shapes are marked adjust to the region Poitou (Vendée, Deux-Sèvres, Vienne). (2) The row ends in 1249 although Alphonse held Poitou to 1271; a keyframe 1250..1271 and the 1271 dissolve are added. The kingdom-of-france dossier has a 1250 gain of Poitou from this slug and a 1271 gain from 'Alfonso, Count of Poitou (apanage)': one of the two should be dropped; overlap with the France leaf shape 1250-1271 should be resolved by the rendering agent. (3) The 1241 shape change has no page; the pages date the grant to 1225.
Not entered (no Cliopatria shape, outside page budget): the Saintonge War (named, undated, on the County of Poitou page); Poitou after 1271, which the pages opened for other states show as the apanage of John, Duke of Berry (Count of Poitou 1356/1357-1416, Berry page infobox 1357, text 1356) and of the future Charles VII (1417-1422, Charles VII page infobox), and which the Treaty of Brétigny list gives to England in 1360. The infobox says 'Merged with the French Crown: 1416'.
Page budget: 1-2 pages; the County of Poitou page is thin (no counts, no dates but 1205), so the Alphonse and County of Auvergne pages were opened. No page gave an infobox area.
